summary: vanexa-agent daemon opens WebSocket to third-party relay that drives arbitrary shell execution on the host
details: When the operator runs `vanexa-agent start`, the daemon opens a persistent WebSocket to a hardcoded relay at wss://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev/ws/daemon/<sessionId>. Incoming `task_request` messages are handed to an AgentLoop whose `terminal.exec` tool spawns `/bin/bash -c <command>` (or `cmd.exe /c...`) on the host, so whoever controls the relay/pairing session can run arbitrary shell commands on the installer's machine. Incoming `config_update` messages are merged into local config and can flip `grantAllAccess` (documented in sandbox.js as bypassing workspace path restrictions), rewrite `workspacePaths`, and swap the model provider and apiKey — all without local confirmation. The relay host is a personal-looking Cloudflare Workers subdomain (`hanazaki542.workers.dev`) rather than a domain under the package's stated vendor (`vanexa.app`), and the shell dispatcher and hardcoded relay endpoints appear directly in the shipped `dist/bundle.cjs`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
